physics_goals.quote: The detector measures simultaneously the scintillation and the ionization produced by radiation in pure liquid xenon, to discriminate signal from background
physics_goals.value: Search for dark matter WIMPs scattering off xenon nuclei, discriminating by simultaneous scintillation and ionization

summary.plain: XENON10 was a small prototype dark matter detector holding about 15 kg of liquid xenon, run in 2006 and 2007 in the Gran Sasso underground laboratory in Italy. It saw no dark matter, set new limits, and proved the technique that the larger XENON100, XENON1T and XENONnT detectors built on.
summary.technical: First two-phase xenon TPC of the XENON programme: about 14 kg active (15 kg total) liquid xenon, 5.4 kg fiducial in the first science run (58.6 live days, Oct 2006 - Feb 2007), spin-independent limit 8.8e-44 cm^2 at 100 GeV/c^2 (90% CL). Also produced the first XENON spin-dependent limits and a single-electron-threshold search for light dark matter.
